items.heading: Here Is the Problem
items.text: Here is the problem with the standard list: it is almost always written at the sector level, not the role level. "Healthcare is growing" tells you nothing about whether a clinical data analyst role in a tier-2 city in India is growing, saturated, or being restructured. "AI is exploding" tells you nothing about whether the specific AI-adjacent role you are considering requires a math PhD or can be entered with a 6-month bootcamp.

items.heading: Every Strong Career Path
items.text: Every strong career path for the next decade traces back to one or more of these structural forces. Understanding them helps you evaluate any career claim, including the ones in .

items.heading: These Paths Are Selected Based
items.text: These paths are selected based on multi-source growth data (WEF 2025, BLS 2024–2034 projections, NASSCOM, industry reports), India salary reality, entry accessibility, and automation resistance. Each card includes a fit signal and an honest caution, because no career is right for everyone.

items.heading: Choosing for Salary Headlines, Not
items.text: Choosing for salary headlines, not job-market fit. Every year, a new salary headline appears, "AI engineers earn $200K!", and thousands of people pivot into AI without checking whether they like the actual work. A high-salary field you dislike compounds into a decade of misalignment. Salary follows market scarcity and demonstrated skill, it is an outcome, not a starting criterion.

items.heading: Waiting for the Perfect Plan
items.text: Waiting for the perfect plan before starting. Most people who are stuck are not stuck because they lack information. They are stuck because the four questions feels overwhelming and they are trying to optimize all four simultaneously before taking any action. Start with Proof 1. Build one project in the most likely path. Adjust from what you learn.

items.heading: Collecting Certificates Instead of Building
items.text: Collecting certificates instead of building proof. A shelf full of online course certificates signals effort, not capability. Employers and clients judge proof of work, real projects, live results, documented decisions. The certificate matters as a learning vehicle, not as a job application item.

items.heading: Confusing a Growing Sector
items.text: Confusing a growing sector with a growing role. Healthcare is growing fast. That does not mean every role in healthcare is growing. The administrative and documentation layer of healthcare is being automated. The clinical, analytical, and systems layer is growing. Always check which layer of the sector you are aiming at.
